notes: Background: mid-market B2B SaaS (developer tools) — chat + docs + code assist embedded in product.
Currently on OpenAI (primary) + small reranking with third-party; primary driver to move: cost predictability + desire for dedicated capacity for consistent latency.
Main asks: drop-in compatibility with current prompt calls, minimal behavior delta, function-calling parity, clear metrics for token accounting.
POC approach: run canonical prompt set (5k) against Redwood hosted + current provider, compare BLEU/ROUGE/embedding similarity + human evaluation for top 200 failure cases.
POC interim: found ~3% regressions concentrated in long-summary prompts and reranking for short answers. SE notes: likely prompt tuning + temp/stop adjustments fix 60% of failures.
Quote from CTO on 2026-02-20 call: "We can't accept systemic regressions on critical support flows; small tuning is fine but need measurable parity before Dedicated."
Compatibility concerns: API parameter names differ (role vs. speaker), function-calling shapes differ; ask: Redwood provide compatibility layer and migration checklist.
Operational: want token-level billing transparency; team requested sample cost run for 3m tokens/day and burst scenarios.
Security/Compliance: require SSO (SAML), audit logs retention 12+ months, KMS integration for key control, data residency option for EU customers.
Next: finish regression triage, deliver PRD for Dedicated sizing, get legal sign-off on residency and SLA.
summary: LatticeCore is a mid-market product SaaS team running a Hosted API POC to validate migration from their current LLM vendor. Primary evaluation axis: prompt parity (behavioral/regression), cost and token accounting, and Dedicated sizing for predictable latency. Success conditions: <1% regressions after prompt-tuning and an agreed compatibility/migration checklist; committed Dedicated contract if pricing and residency clauses acceptable.
